story_type: moon landing nearly aborted by an engine fault in lunar orbit, 1972 mission film
hook: The Moon was right below them. The landing was almost off.
narration: The Moon was right below them, and their landing was almost called off.
April 1972. On Apollo 16, John Young and Charlie Duke had just undocked their lunar module.
Ken Mattingly, alone in the command module, was about to fire its main engine.
Getting ready, he found oscillations in the engine's backup control system. Following mission rules, he did not burn.
That engine was the one they needed to leave lunar orbit and get home, so nobody could guess about it.
The two spacecraft stayed close, ready to dock if needed. The chances for a landing looked pretty slim.
Teams in Houston, Massachusetts and Southern California worked the problem and ran simulator tests.
The tests showed that with the engine on, the oscillations would do no harm.
[short pause] On revolution sixteen, Young and Duke got a go for another try.
outcome: Young and Duke landed on the Descartes plateau after a near abort that lasted six hours.
title: Apollo 16 landing almost called off
description:
On April 20, 1972, an engine control problem in Apollo 16's command module nearly cancelled the Moon landing. After six hours of tests and analysis, John Young and Charlie Duke got a go and landed at Descartes. From the 1972 NASA film Apollo 16: Nothing So Hidden.
